facts.fact: UNCTAD's Cyberlaw Tracker lists Law No. 2016-031 among Madagascar's cybercrime legislation (law year 2016; survey round 2026-11-10).
Amnesty International says the government proposed a cybercrime law in August 2026 giving it new powers to monitor online activity and permanent access to telecom data without judicial oversight.
The Presidency recalled that article 20 of law 2014-006 on cybercrime, as amended by law 2016-031, sets fines of Ar 2 million to 100 million for insulting officials.
The Presidency said on 8 January 2026 that prosecutions were under way against people, accounts or pages for online insults and hate against senior officials.

L'Express de Madagascar reports the government withdrew the cybercrime bill from the National Assembly's agenda in November 2026, at the same time as the electronic communications bill, so it is a bill not yet passed.
Tech-Connect says Law n°2014-006 on cybercrime is currently in force in Madagascar and defines offences such as fraudulent access to an information system.
Tech-Connect says bill 042/2026, a 96-article replacement cybercrime law, had its National Assembly examination postponed sine die as at 5 September 2026.
